scenario: cacheFile target escaping the tool folder
reason: CacheFile strips leading '..' and '.' segments from the target so that a target can never be written outside the tool folder; @actions/tool-cache joins the path verbatim and writes ../escaped.txt next to the architecture folder. Deliberate hardening, kept.

CacheOptions.Tool is validated and an error is returned; @actions/tool-cache accepts '' and caches straight into the root of the tool cache. Kept: the Go options struct makes an unset field indistinguishable from an empty one.

CacheOptions.Version is validated and an error is returned; @actions/tool-cache accepts '' and caches into <tool>/<arch>. Kept: an unset field is indistinguishable from an empty one in the Go options struct.
Same as 'cacheDir empty tool name': CacheOptions.Tool is validated in Go.
Same as 'cacheDir empty version': CacheOptions.Version is validated in Go.

scenario: downloadTool redirect with a relative location
reason: Go follows a relative Location header as RFC 9110 requires; @actions/http-client passes it to new URL() and fails with 'Invalid URL' (retried three times). Reference bug, not reproduced.

scenario: extractTar an absolute symlink out of the destination
reason: Security hardening, kept: tar creates the link as is (here to /etc/passwd), ExtractTar refuses a symbolic link whose target is absolute or leaves the destination, skips the member, extracts the rest and fails with the exit code 2 error of tar.

scenario: extractTar a relative symlink out of the destination
reason: Same hardening as 'an absolute symlink out of the destination' for a target that climbs out of dest with '..'.

scenario: extractTar a member written through a symlink out of the destination
reason: Consequence of the symlink hardening: the link l is not created, so the member l/pwned.txt becomes a plain file in a new directory l, where tar (which created the link and then refused to write through it) extracts nothing. Nothing is ever written outside of dest by either.

Transport errors carry the text of the runtime (node: 'connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:1', Go: 'Get "...": dial tcp ...: connection refused'); the retry flow and the log lines around the message are identical.
